newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglovaal sees increase in 96/97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Anglovaal sees increase in 96/97 earnings.

text.p: Anglovaal Ltd said on Thursday group earnings in the 1996/97 financial year were expected to increase as the contributions from its underlying industrial and mining companies grew.
"Industrial company earnings should grow as...cost-saving and restructuring measures...begin to take effect," Anglovaal said in a statement accompanying its results for the year ended June 30, 1996.

It said programmes were underway at a number of companies in the Anglovaal Industries Ltd stable to cut operating costs and improve focus after they experienced tough trading conditions in the second half of the financial year.

These programmes included the implementation of an extensive transformation process at food and retail business National Brands, major capital investments at packaging business Consol Ltd's glass plants and the partial unbundling of construction firm Grinaker Holdings.

Another cost-cutting programme was the proposed merger of cement concern Alpha Ltd with competitor Blue Circle. The Competition Board last week said it would recommend to government to block the planned tie-up.

Anglovaal said earnings from mining operations were likely to rise with the commencement of profitable new operations and higher contributions from Saturn, whose income is based on royalties received the Venetia diamond mine.
Venetia is operated by De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.
It said "encouraging progress" was being made in the development of the Target gold project, the Nkomati nickel operation, the Forzando coal project and in the Zambian copper belt.
Anglovaal on Thursday reported an 18 percent rise in earnings before exceptional items to 784 cents a share in the year to end-June. The dividend was increased 24 percent to 183 cents a share.
